finding.claim: With the permitSetMultiParamEntries option enabled, object parameter keys are interpolated into the SQL inside backticks with no escaping. Values are escaped, but keys are not. If an application passes an attacker-influenced object (for example a parsed JSON request body) as the parameter of `SET ?` or `INSERT ... SET ?`, a key containing a backtick breaks out of the identifier and allows SQL injection. This is the same class of bug as the well-known mysql `SET ?` object-key injection. It only applies when the option is enabled, which is opt-in.
finding.source: Keys of a JS object passed as a query parameter (e.g. req.body) when opts.permitSetMultiParamEntries is true, e.g. {"a`=1, role=`admin": 1}.
finding.sink: out.writeString('`' + key + '`') writes the unescaped key into the text-protocol SQL sent to the server.

trace.note: opts.permitSetMultiParamEntries branch reached for a plain object that is not Date, Buffer, Array or GeoJSON
for (let key in value) iterates attacker-controlled keys, including inherited enumerable ones
key is concatenated between backticks and written to the output without doubling embedded backticks

finding.guards_checked: Looked for backtick escaping or key validation in text-encoder.js and packet-output-stream.js, and found none. writeString does no SQL escaping. The value path (line 137) goes through writeParam and is escaped, including the NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES handling. The option is opt-in and off by default, so exposure depends on application usage. The binary-protocol encoder does not use this path.
